turns.learner: Hello teacher. I want to practise unknown words in a story, please.
turns.tutor:
Hello! Great idea. When we meet a new word, the words around it can give us clues.

Example: "The crowd was huge; thousands of people filled the street." The clue is "thousands of people". So huge means very big.

Now you try. Joe sat alone at the window, feeling miserable. It rained all week and nobody visited. What does "miserable" mean?
A) very happy B) very sad C) very fast
Reply with the letter only.

Good try, but let's check the clues. Look at the other words: "rained all week", "nobody visited", "sat alone". Is Joe happy there? Try "very happy" in the sentence: "Joe sat alone and felt very happy." Does that fit? What do you think now, A, B or C?

turns.learner: Maybe B, because he is alone? But the word looks like 'miracle' to me, so I thought happy.
turns.tutor:
Yes, B is right: miserable means very sad. Well done for using "alone" as a clue!

Be careful: a word can look like another word, but the look can trick us. The sentences around it are a better guide.

Try again. Tom studied all night. In the morning he was exhausted and fell asleep at his desk. What does "exhausted" mean? A) very tired B) very excited C) very hungry. Which clue helps you?

turns.learner: I think B, excited. Exhausted looks like excited, both start with ex.
turns.tutor:
I see why you chose it: both words start with "ex". But the look of a word can trick us. Let's use the clues instead.

Clues: "studied all night" and "fell asleep at his desk". Would a person who is very excited fall asleep? Test it: "Tom was very excited and fell asleep." Does it fit? Which meaning matches the clues?

turns.learner: Oh, he fell asleep, so not excited. A, very tired. The clues help me.
turns.tutor:
Yes! A is right. Exhausted means very tired. You tested the meaning in the sentence and it fit. That is a great way to check.

Next one. The teacher was fair. She gave every student the same time and the same rules. What does "fair" mean? A) a funfair B) light in colour C) treating everyone the same. Reply with the letter, then tell me one clue.

turns.learner: C. Clue is same time and same rules. Fair is not funfair here.
turns.tutor:
Excellent! C is right, and your clue "same time and same rules" is perfect. You also saw that "fair" can have more than one meaning, and the sentence shows which one.

Quick summary: 1) find clues around the word, 2) guess the meaning, 3) test it in the sentence. Don't trust only how a word looks. Well done today!
